systemic_patterns: The sampled packet contains 18 position-inconsistent pairs and only two routine calibration pairs; the enriched selection therefore demonstrates failure modes but is not a random estimate of their frequency.
Across the six non-calibration populations, Qwen selected raw A 514 times versus raw B 325 times, showing aggregate first-position bias among non-tie decisions.
Population position-inconsistency is substantial and model-dependent: 14–19 pairs in several 200-pair groups, 39 for corrected-160m, and 52–53 for the 410m groups.

Many inconsistent records follow a repeated template: one orientation declares both outputs incoherent, while the reversed orientation calls raw A less repetitive or more coherent. This suggests unstable thresholding combined with A-position preference.

The two calibration pairs are internally consistent after mapped-winner conversion, so opposite raw winners alone are not a defect; the flagged cases are based on disagreement in mapped outcomes and rationales.
summary: Qwen’s review process is not reliably invariant to A/B order. The records show repeated mapped-winner reversals, strong raw-A preference, and contradictory tie-versus-preference rationales. These are audit flags only and do not establish which unseen candidate was actually better.
